data.name: The Marquee: Lights. Camera. Legacy.
data.detailed_description:
Build a studio. Make your films. Leave your mark on cinema.

Begin with limited resources and a vision for the films you want to make. Name your studio, develop its capabilities, and guide it through a changing film industry. Build your reputation through commercial hits, prestige pictures, ambitious experiments, or a catalogue that embraces them all.

Every production starts with a screenplay. Combine genres and themes, develop your ideas, and decide which projects deserve further investment. Refine a screenplay before committing to production, balancing creative ambition against the money, people, and facilities available to you.

Research expands your options. Develop your studio’s knowledge, explore production techniques, and prepare for projects that demand more from your company. Choose where to invest today and what kind of filmmaker you want to become tomorrow.

Find the people who bring your stories to life.

Scout actors and directors, compare their abilities and costs, and assemble the team for your next film. Balance established names against emerging talent, consider availability, and decide where a stronger cast or creative team justifies the expense.

Portrait-led conversations bring studio decisions and industry encounters into focus. Guided tutorial lessons introduce the work of running your company, from developing a screenplay to producing and releasing a film.

Take your production from the page to the screen.

Greenlighting a film turns an idea into a financial commitment. Choose your production approach, organise preparation, and manage the project as it moves towards release.

Budgets, schedules, staffing, and production decisions all compete for your attention. Respond to setbacks and opportunities, weigh the cost of changing course, and decide how much risk your studio can afford.

Your next project must also survive in a wider industry. Rival studios release their own films, pursue audiences, and shape the market around you. Follow the competition and consider where your film fits before choosing its release window.

Find an audience—and understand the result.

Plan marketing and distribution, then follow your film’s theatrical performance. Compare critical reception, audience response, ticket sales, revenue, and costs to understand what a release means for your studio.

A good review does not pay every bill. A strong opening does not tell the whole story. Use charts, financial information, and your growing release history to judge which decisions worked and where your next production should change.

Explore cinema ownership and management, and develop merchandise connected to your films and characters as your business grows.

Build a catalogue worth returning to.

Continue a story with a sequel, develop a spin-off, or pursue an original idea. Create and develop franchise characters, follow audience interest, and decide when an established property deserves another film.

Each release becomes part of your studio’s history. Success can create room for a larger production, while a disappointment may force you to rethink your plans. Balance familiar properties with new ideas as you build a company with its own creative identity.

Across changing cinematic eras, adapt your choices, develop talent, and keep your studio moving forward. Your legacy grows through the films you release and the decisions you make between them.

Features

  • Build and develop your own film studio.

  • Create screenplays using multiple genres and themes.

  • Refine projects before committing them to production.

  • Scout and hire talent, balancing ability, availability, and cost.

  • Manage production preparation, budgets, schedules, and creative decisions.

  • Research genres, themes, technologies, and studio capabilities.

  • Experience portrait-led conversations and guided tutorial lessons.

  • Compete in a film industry with rival studios and competing releases.

  • Plan marketing, distribution, and theatrical release timing.

  • Follow reviews, audience response, box office performance, and studio finances.

  • Develop sequels, spin-offs, franchise characters, and merchandise.

  • Explore cinema ownership and management.

  • Save your campaign and continue building your studio’s history.

AI artwork disclosure: A small amount of artwork was created using AI tools. I intend to replace this artwork in time. Portraits are made using real photography/images and then edited to suit the game's style. sources available
